summary.en: Violent clashes continue across South Sudan, with government forces and SPLA-IO fighting in Wij-Panyikang, Upper Nile, and communal violence in Tonj North killing dozens. The government reported a 72‑person death toll in Tonj North, while victims of the Akol Koor residence clash are seeking over $340,000 in compensation from the Defence Ministry. Riek Machar denied commanding the White Army in court, and the South Sudan Bar Association launched a roadmap to improve access to justice. Canada emphasized media freedom as essential for peace, and the government and UN set a 2026 resettlement target after assisting 28,000 people since January. Two battle-related deaths were recorded in 2024, according to UCDP.
summary.nb: Voldelige sammenstøt fortsetter over hele Sør-Sudan, med regjeringsstyrker og SPLA-IO i kamp i Wij-Panyikang i Upper Nile, og kommunal vold i Tonj North som har drept dusinvis. Regjeringen rapporterte 72 døde i Tonj North, mens ofrene for sammenstøtet ved Akol Koor-boligen krever over 340 000 dollar i erstatning fra Forsvarsdepartementet. Riek Machar benektet å ha kommandert White Army i retten, og Sør-Sudans advokatforening lanserte en veikart for å bedre rettstilgangen. Canada understreket mediefrihet som essensielt for fred, og regjeringen og FN satte et mål om bosetting i 2026 etter å ha bistått 28 000 personer siden januar. To dødsfall knyttet til kamper ble registrert i 2024, ifølge UCDP.

background.title: South Sudanese Civil War
background.extract: The South Sudanese Civil War was a multi-sided civil war in South Sudan fought from 2013 to 2018 between government and opposition forces. The civil war caused rampant human rights abuses, including forced displacement, ethnic massacres, and killings of journalists by various parties. Since the war's end, South Sudan has been governed by a coalition formed by leaders of the former warring factions, Salva Kiir Mayardit and Riek Machar. The country continues to recover from the war while experiencing ongoing and systemic ethnic violence.
